sources.entry: qBittorrent | BitTorrent client with a web UI

summary.one_liner: A Docker container image packaging the qBittorrent BitTorrent client with its web UI, maintained by the LinuxServer.io team.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a containerized qBittorrent client (C++/Qt, built on libtorrent) that exposes a web UI on port 8080 by default. The admin password is printed to the container log at first startup and should be changed in the web UI settings. Ports for the web UI and the torrenting connection (TCP and UDP) can be changed through WEBUI_PORT and TORRENTING_PORT variables. Volumes map a config directory and a downloads directory, with PUID/PGID for host file permissions. Two tags are offered: latest (libtorrent v2) and libtorrentv1. Images are published for amd64 and arm64.
use_cases: Run a torrent client on a home server or NAS
Download torrents through a browser-based web UI
Manage BitTorrent downloads in a Docker Compose stack
Run qBittorrent with a read-only or non-root container
Choose between libtorrent v1 and v2 builds
how_to_run: docker-compose: define the qbittorrent service with image lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:latest, environment PUID/PGID/TZ/WEBUI_PORT/TORRENTING_PORT, volumes for /config and /downloads, and ports 8080, 6881 tcp and 6881 udp
Or use docker run -d --name=qbittorrent with the same -e, -p and -v flags
Read the container log (docker logs -f qbittorrent) to find the temporary admin password
Log in to the web UI on port 8080 and change the username and password
notable: Multi-arch images for x86-64 and arm64 via a Docker manifest
Choice of libtorrent v2 (latest) or libtorrent v1 (libtorrentv1 tag)
Supports PUID/PGID user mapping and FILE__ environment variables from Docker secrets
Optional UMASK setting and read-only or non-root operation
Built on a custom base image with s6 overlay and regular rebuilds
caveats: If the web UI password is not changed, a new one is generated every time the container starts
Changing the web UI port requires updating both the port mapping and WEBUI_PORT
An active torrenting port needs to be opened on the host; the README notes this can differ from the internal port
armhf is deprecated; only amd64 and arm64 are supported
